result.title: Cross-Attack Robust Aggregation for Federated Learning
result.summary: Federated learning (FL) lets resource-constrained IoT and edge devices train a shared model without exchanging raw data, but compromised or faulty devices can poison the global model. Existing robust aggregators each fail in some regime: naive averaging (FedAvg) collapses under high-magnitude attacks, whereas distance- and statistics-based defenses (Krum, median, trimmed mean) sacrifice accuracy on non-IID data and remain vulnerable to stealthy attacks. We present FedTether, which reweights client updates by their deviation from a coordinatewise median through a robust, dead-zoned score applied as a server-side optimizer step. Across three datasets, three attack types, and Byzantine fractions up to 40%, FedTether is the only method top-tier in every regime: it matches FedAvg under stealthy attacks with no robustness tax, exceeds robust baselines by up to 42 accuracy points, and stays accurate where high-magnitude attacks reduce FedAvg to near-random. These properties persist at 50 clients under partial participation, with no shared data or validation set.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究联邦学习中恶意或故障客户端带来的投毒问题，提出 FedTether：按客户端更新相对坐标中位数的偏离计算带死区的鲁棒分数进行重加权，并作为服务端优化步骤，在多数据集、多攻击类型与部分参与条件下兼顾鲁棒性与精度。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关联，但「偏离中位数即降权」的鲁棒聚合与免鲁棒性代价的评价思路，可能启发多 latent 假设或视觉证据筛选时对不可靠来源的加权取舍，属较远领域迁移，需核查其在高维状态聚合下的可用性。
